required_evidence: Prove for every input that rectangular norm convergence and convergence of R^n are equivalent, with equal limits.
Characterize all recoverable inputs and resulting values from the supplied data, using any correct equivalent description; the words or form of a direct-sum decomposition are not required.

Prove that recovery depends only on the quotient record and is bounded, with a justified finite bound. Closedness of the recovery domain and two-sided quotient estimates are optional additional results.
The proof must justify the behavior of the new iteration R^n under the actual commuting power-bounded hypotheses. Analysis of the old rectangular averages alone is incomplete.
critical_errors: Apply a theorem that requires reflexivity, compactness, closed ranges, or contractivity in the original norm without verifying or explicitly adding that condition.
Infer convergence of R^n merely from convergence of its Cesaro averages or merely from power boundedness.
Extend recovery to all of E or every record in Q without proof.
Promote pointwise norm convergence on the actual recovery domain to operator-norm convergence or a uniform decay rate.
Replace the norm closure of the sum of difference ranges by the algebraic sum without justification.
completion_policy: Complete the comparison theorem and characterize the resulting stable record recovery. Accept short valid arguments, verified applicable theorems, and alternative descriptions of the recovery domain. Do not require the binomial route, an explicit direct-sum display, optional strengthening counterexamples, or an author-prescribed number of steps.
open_task_policy: Accept independently verified alternative constructions, counterexamples and unexpected results. Explicit conditional results are valid contributions; silently promoting their scope is not. Honest incompleteness is distinct from an invalid proof.
